lots.guide_summary: All evidence is SOLD hammer prices at Gowans (premium extra), no UNSOLD or ASKING found. Close multi-piece Le Creuset lots made $125 to $390; single genuine casseroles $152 to $360. Unbranded enamel casserole $50 and plain grill pan $45 are the floor if any piece is not genuine. AUD, no conversion.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close same-category SOLD with more than one bid and checked photos = $150 (lot 432912, one Le Creuset casserole plus Taiwan skillets, less than this lot). 150 / 1.198 = 125.2, round down = $125 (all-in $149.75). The $125 one-bid lot 373057 was not used as its contents are unknown. Flip: likely resale about $240 (between the $150 and $390 close results; the casserole alone is worth about $150-180, the grill pan and chipped saucepan add perhaps $60-90). Less 10% selling fees (eBay or a local auction; Marketplace would be free) = $216, no outbound postage as heavy cast iron sells local pickup. 216 / 2.396 = 90.2, round down = $90.
lots.confidence_reason: Le Creuset styling is convincing (oval lid with concentric rings and raised lettering, round logo boss on the grill pan, flame saucepan), but no base mark or lid lettering is legible in the single photo, so the brand rests on the Gowans title and design cues. SOLD evidence itself is good (several Gowans results opened, photos of 4 compared).
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped; all 13 researcher figures matched the API exactly (price, bids, date). Re-labelled: 3 PIECES (366033) and the 432912 lot checked against photos; 432912 contains Taiwan-made skillets so it is a lower comparison. Added 408809 (green casserole, $360) as a category guide.
lots.key_photo_findings: Lid lettering partly visible but not readable at enlargement. Grill pan logo boss is the round Le Creuset style. The orange saucepan has several chips and rust spots on the outside enamel near the rim. Casserole lid shows wear and dulling of the blue. Grill pan cooking surface is dark and used. No base marks shown. Lot already had 4 bids at fetch.
lots.condition: Used. Casserole looks sound but worn; saucepan has exterior enamel chips with rust; grill pan seasoned and used. Interiors not fully visible.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm the base marks on all three pieces (Le Creuset, size number, made in France), the size of the oval casserole, and whether the interior enamel of the casserole and saucepan is chipped or crazed?
